criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Include the following required information: What is the spacecraft's primary mission? Why is the mission needed? How many spacecraft are used and why? Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: All required elements are thoroughly addressed with specific detail and relevant literature citations. The mission concept and rationale directly benefit Australia.

evidence.quote: The primary mission of ZYZZsat is to image the whole Great Barrier Reef in visible bands at 5 m resolution
One satellite is therefore used. This also simplifies communications, reduces cost, and requires less time to build and launch.
The operator is the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS)... The customers are the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority

criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Demonstrates an excellent understanding of mission design. Calculations for launch azimuth, J2 sun-synchronous inclination, imaging geometry, communications data budget, and passive orbital decay are accurate and rigorously supported by STK outputs.

evidence.quote: The baseline is an SSMS rideshare flight on Vega C from Kourou in early 2025
Table 4: Orbital elements of ZYZZsat at the scenario epoch, 3 Feb 2025 00:00:00 UTCG
The Mount Pleasant Radio Observatory near Hobart, Tasmania (42.8°S, 147.4°E) is selected.
The mission lasts five years... The EOL plan is therefore passive: a drag sail is deployed

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: The conclusion synthesises findings thoroughly, reiterates quantitative performance metrics, and offers critical engineering insight into four realistic design limitations.

evidence.quote: ZYZZsat meets the mission needs set out in the introduction with one 50 kg satellite.
The design has four limitations. First, Vega C has not yet flown... Second, fluid lensing has only been demonstrated

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Exemplary presentation. The document features an executive summary, clear heading hierarchy, well-formatted tables, appropriately referenced figures, clean STK screenshots, and correct citation formatting throughout.

overall: An outstanding submission that meets all requirements to an exceptional standard. Technical derivations, orbital mechanics, STK simulations, and payload tradeoffs are executed with rigour and clarity.

feedback.summary: You have produced an exceptional mission design report, achieving full marks across all criteria. Your technical derivations, orbital mechanics analysis, and seamless integration of STK simulations set a benchmark for rigorous engineering documentation. Every mission requirement is thoroughly justified, clearly communicated, and directly linked to Australian stakeholder needs.
next_steps: Investigate active deorbiting alternatives alongside passive drag sails to assess mass tradeoffs under varying solar activity cycles.
Formulate a quantitative risk-mitigation plan addressing the Vega-C flight heritage and unproven fluid lensing technology identified in Section 3.
Explore multi-ground-station network options to increase downlink margins and reduce onboard data storage constraints.

criteria.C1: You achieved Accomplished by delivering a compelling mission rationale in Section 1. Defining AIMS as the operator, GBRMPA as the customer, and justifying a single-satellite architecture provided excellent context and national benefit.
criteria.C2: You reached Accomplished through rigorous mission analysis across Section 2. Your launch vehicle trade study, J2 orbital derivations, Mount Pleasant ground link budget, and passive deorbit calculations were comprehensively validated with STK simulation files.
criteria.C3: You earned Accomplished in Section 3 by clearly synthesising your quantitative outcomes. Honestly evaluating realistic mission constraints, including Vega-C launch readiness and fluid-lensing payload maturity, demonstrated outstanding engineering maturity.
criteria.C4: You met the Accomplished level with flawless technical presentation. The report featured a succinct Executive Summary, professional heading hierarchy, pristine data tables, clear STK visualisations, and consistent academic referencing throughout.
